ambrosia.storage_change: Crispness fades quickly at room temperature, when it can turn slightly pear-like; best kept chilled (Orange Pippin).

climate_flavour.note: Wikipedia: colours differently in warmer climates (colour, not flavour).

ambrosia.notes: floral not supported by either source.

antonovka.notes: perfumed not supported by any modern source. Orange Pippin and Wikipedia both describe Antonovka as a group/population of related forms.

arthur-turner.peak: Aug-Oct (Chris Bowers nursery: 'for eating August to October').
arthur-turner.notes: NFC page (id 224) and Chris Bowers nursery page give no flavour words, so not counted.

ballyfatten.storage_change: Tart straight from the tree; sweetens (quickly, per Wikipedia) in store and can then be eaten raw.
ballyfatten.peak: Oct-Dec from store (Future Forests: pick late Sept, keeps Oct-Dec).

beauty-of-kent.notes: Not on Orange Pippin. Wikipedia page exists but has no flavour words.

berner-rosen.peak: From late September off the tree; keeps to January, longer from higher-altitude sites (de.wikipedia).
berner-rosen.notes: de.wikipedia compares the aroma to raspberry (himbeerartig) and calls it sweet-vinous-acid.

blenheim-orange.peak: Cooking from late September; eating from October to January (Wikipedia).

braddick-nonpareil.storage_change: Intensely sharp, even eye-watering, when just picked; sweetens in store, a good winter keeper (Orange Pippin).
braddick-nonpareil.notes: Orange Pippin page is under the slug braddicks-nonpareil. Orange Pippin stresses sharpness; NFC calls it sweet and aromatic.

browns-apple.notes: Trees of Antiquity classes it as a bittersharp; OP and NFC call it a sharp (no tannin mentioned).

captain-kidd.notes: Orange Pippin page exists but has no description. Wikipedia 'Captain Kidd' redirects to Kidd's Orange Red (the parent) - not counted. honey, pear-drop and wine not supported.

cherry-cox.notes: Orange Pippin has only attribute fields, no prose. floral, pear-drop, honey and nutty not supported by modern sources.

cockle-pippin.notes: Not on Orange Pippin; no Wikipedia page.

costard.notes: NFC lists three Costards: (1) the medieval apple (subacid, tender, probably no longer grown), (2) and (3) 1883 exhibits from Hereford/Gloucestershire, (3) 'acid' - probably different apples. Wikipedia (Costard (apple)) says only that it was thought to be a cooking apple; no flavour words.

darcy-spice.storage_change: Hard and sharp when picked; historically stored a month or two before eating, when (after a good year) it sweetens and develops its sweet-spice, mince-pie character (Orange Pippin).

climate_flavour.note: Orange Pippin: in cooler or less sunny parts of the UK it may not ripen properly and is poorly flavoured; best in the warmer, drier East/South-East.

darcy-spice.peak: After 1-2 months in store; keeps to the following spring (Orange Pippin).
darcy-spice.notes: cinnamon appears only inside Orange Pippin's mince-pie analogy (apple, cinnamon and raisins); Trees of Antiquity says nutmeg. Scott Farm (4th source, not counted) also says nutmeg and best after storage.

dolgo.notes: Orange Pippin page has no flavour words; NFC does not hold it. Scott Farm (orchard) and Trees of Antiquity (nursery) are separate organisations.

duke-of-devonshire.notes: Wikipedia page has no flavour words. pear-drop, sweet and sharp not supported by modern sources.

ecklinville.peak: Sept-Oct (Future Forests: pick early Sept, keeps Sept-Oct).
ecklinville.notes: Disagreement: NFC 'very acid'; Future Forests 'not too sharp'.

fall-pippin.peak: Ripens Aug-Sept; favoured as an early winter apple (Big Horse Creek Farm).
fall-pippin.notes: Orange Pippin has only attribute fields, no prose.

foxwhelp-broxwood.notes: Not on Orange Pippin. Trees of Antiquity and Scott Farm have pages for plain 'Foxwhelp' (bittersharp; earthy, pear, butterscotch hints in cider), not the Broxwood sport - not counted.

climate_flavour.note: Needs lots of sunshine to ripen properly (Orange Pippin); thrives with relatively warm summers (Wikipedia); often fails to mature fully in the UK (NFC).

fuji.peak: Nov-Dec in the northern hemisphere (Orange Pippin); keeps very long (Wikipedia).
fuji.notes: honey not supported by these sources.

gladstone.storage_change: Crisp and juicy at first but soon goes soft (NFC); keeps only 1-3 days (Orange Pippin).
gladstone.peak: Early August, straight from the tree.
gladstone.notes: Orange Pippin has only attribute fields, no prose.

golden-knob.notes: Not on Orange Pippin; no Wikipedia page. Specialty Produce has a page but was not used (its wording may derive from Keepers Nursery).

climate_flavour.note: Orange Pippin: needs a warm climate to ripen properly; green colour needs warm days and nights (cold nights give a blush).

granny-smith.notes: lemon not supported by any source. NFC is milder ('subacid, moderately sweet') than OP/Wikipedia. Orange Pippin also quotes a Californian grower: left on the tree into winter it yellows and the acidity mellows.

hambledon-deux-ans.notes: Not on Orange Pippin; no Wikipedia page.

howgate-wonder.storage_change: Sweetens towards the end of its storage period, when it can be eaten as a dessert apple (Future Forests).
howgate-wonder.peak: Keeps as late as March (Future Forests).

climate_flavour.note: Orange Pippin: good red colour is key to the Jazz flavour; poorly coloured fruit tastes like Braeburn.

jazz.peak: Northern-hemisphere fruit in shops Nov-Dec (Orange Pippin).
jazz.notes: banana not supported. Third source is the brand owner's (ENZA) consumer site.

jumbo.storage_change: Keeps very well: fruit put in a fridge in early October was still being eaten in early March with virtually no loss, and later in the season it can be eaten as a dessert apple (Chris Bowers).
jumbo.notes: Assumed the Chris Bowers 'Jumbo' cooking apple is our Jumbo (no other information to confirm). Not on Orange Pippin, NFC or Wikipedia.

kentish-quarrenden.notes: NFC: received by the National Fruit Trials before 1931, origin unknown. Not on Orange Pippin; no Wikipedia page.

kingston-black.notes: Wikipedia also reports doubts that its vintage reputation is 'somewhat exaggerated' and Hogg's source saying it alone makes a thin cider.

lady-williams.storage_change: Tart if harvested early; mellows when left on the tree into early winter (Trees of Antiquity).

climate_flavour.note: Very well suited to warm climates and unlikely to ripen in cooler ones (Orange Pippin); rarely reaches maturity in the UK (NFC); suited to low-chill sites (Trees of Antiquity).

lady-williams.peak: Very late; picked as late as February in southern California (Orange Pippin).
lady-williams.notes: NFC and Wikipedia pages give no flavour words.

london-pippin.notes: Orange Pippin page (five-crown-pippin) has no description. NFC text says 'acid flesh' but its field says 'subacid'.

magnum-bonum.peak: Ripens Sept-Oct, keeps fairly well (Big Horse Creek Farm).
magnum-bonum.notes: NFC record is named 'Bonum' (Davidson County, North Carolina, Squire Kinney) - matches Magnum Bonum's origin. Orange Pippin page describes a 'yellow' apple with no flavour words - not counted. sweet and sharp not supported.

mcintosh-red.storage_change: Keeps reasonably but the vinous flavour fades quickly in store (Orange Pippin); can turn mealy if stored below 2 C (Wikipedia).

climate_flavour.note: Best flavour in colder apple regions (Orange Pippin); grows best where nights are cold and autumn days clear, otherwise poor colour and soft flesh (Wikipedia).

mcintosh-red.peak: Straight from the tree, mid-September onwards.

michaelmas-red.notes: Not on Orange Pippin under either name.

newton-wonder.notes: Stores very well (Orange Pippin) but no source describes a flavour change in store.

northern-spy.peak: Picked late Oct-early Nov and used through the winter; keeps into spring in cold store (Orange Pippin).

otava.notes: Not on Orange Pippin; NFC record exists but variety is not held and has no description; no en/de/cs Wikipedia article; a web search found no usable grower page.

pecks-pleasant.peak: Ripens Sept-Oct; turns yellow with a blush in store (Big Horse Creek Farm).
pecks-pleasant.notes: Scott Farm's page (not counted) repeats Orange Pippin's wording and adds that it improves with keeping into deep winter.

pixie.storage_change: Sharper than Cox just after picking; mellows in store and the flavour can improve up to Dec/Jan (Orange Pippin, Future Forests).
pixie.peak: Dec-Jan after storage; keeps to March (Orange Pippin, Future Forests).

primrose-pippin.notes: Not on Orange Pippin, NFC or Wikipedia; two web searches found no page for a 'Primrose Pippin' apple (only Christmas Pippin and King of the Pippins).

rave.storage_change: Pleasantly tart when picked early, well balanced at full maturity; stores up to 6 months (University of Minnesota).

climate_flavour.note: Wikipedia: fruit quality depends on climate, site and growing practice; Stemilt credits long sunny days in central Washington for its colour.

rave.peak: Mid-Aug to early Sept in Minnesota (UMN); sold Aug-Oct (Stemilt).
rave.notes: Not on Orange Pippin or NFC. Stemilt is the licensed grower/marketer.

red-sauce.peak: Harvest late Sept-early Oct, keeps until November (Chris Bowers).
red-sauce.notes: Orange Pippin page has no description. mild not clearly supported (NFC only 'subacid').

reverend-w-wilks.notes: perfumed and mild not supported. Chris Bowers page (cooks to a golden froth) has no flavour words.

roxbury-russet.storage_change: Good winter keeper; Wikipedia cites the old belief that it improves with age.
roxbury-russet.notes: spice and honey not supported. Trees of Antiquity: don't pick too early or the sugars fail to develop. Wikipedia has no flavour words. Scott Farm (4th, not counted) likens it to sweet guava and persimmon with coconut.

saltcote-pippin.notes: Not on Orange Pippin; no Wikipedia page.

scrumptious.peak: From the tree from early September; keeps through October (Chris Bowers); keeps about a week (Orange Pippin).
scrumptious.notes: NFC page has no flavour description. Chris Bowers reports descriptions by others ('variously described as').

siberian-crab.notes: Orange Pippin (ornamental), Wikipedia (Malus baccata: fruit edible) and Trees of Antiquity (good colour and flavour for pickles, jelly, cider) give no flavour words; NFC does not list it.

somerset-redstreak.notes: Not on Orange Pippin; no Wikipedia page.

stirling-castle.peak: August-September, keeps 2-3 weeks (Orange Pippin, quoting Hogg).

swaar.storage_change: Best after mellowing 4-6 weeks in store, when it softens and the flavour 'explodes' (Trees of Antiquity).
swaar.peak: After 4-6 weeks in store; keeps 3-6 months (Trees of Antiquity).
swaar.notes: nutty not supported by the three counted sources; Scott Farm (4th, not counted) says complex and nutty after some weeks in refrigerated storage.

ten-commandments.notes: Not on Orange Pippin; no Wikipedia page. NFC's 'sweet but acid' sits badly with our 'mild'.

transparente-de-croncels.storage_change: Keeps no more than about a month (de.wikipedia).

climate_flavour.note: de.wikipedia: aroma ranges from slight to fine depending on site; in a rough climate the fruit does not ripen.

transparente-de-croncels.notes: Not on Orange Pippin. mild not explicitly supported (both say gently sweet-sour).

virginia-beauty.peak: Oct-Feb; a good keeper (Big Horse Creek Farm).
virginia-beauty.notes: Not on Orange Pippin, NFC or Wikipedia. sweet not supported by the one source found.

white-transparent.storage_change: Soon becomes woolly and dry (NFC); keeps about a week (Orange Pippin).
white-transparent.peak: Late July-August, straight from the tree.
white-transparent.notes: Orange Pippin treats White and Yellow Transparent as one; Wikipedia says Yellow Transparent is sometimes described differently (fine flesh, sub-acid). NFC also has a separate 'Papirovka' accession described as acid.

winter-pearmain.notes: Orange Pippin page has attribute fields only, no flavour words; no Wikipedia page.

yates.peak: Ripens October and keeps very well until April (Big Horse Creek Farm).
yates.notes: Orange Pippin page has no flavour words. citrus not supported.

zuccalmaglios-renette.notes: Orange Pippin page (zuccalmaglios-reinette) has no flavour words. de.wikipedia calls it juicy, NFC rather dry.
